QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_12

question.text: The exchange-level open interest in GOI bond futures on a long-maturity bucket underlying is Rs. 20,000 crores, with a Rs. 400 crore floor for that bucket. What is the client-level position limit applicable to a client in this bond future?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per pages 234-236 of the NISM Series IV workbook, GOI bond futures client-level position limits are set as a percentage of open interest or a maturity-bucket floor amount, whichever is higher. Applying 3% of exchange open interest = 3% x Rs. 20,000 crore = Rs. 600 crore. Comparing with the Rs. 400 crore floor for the bucket: Rs. 600 crore is higher, so the client-level limit is Rs. 600 crore. The Trap: Rs. 400 crore would apply only if the percentage calculation came out lower than the floor; the workbook uses whichever is higher, not lower. Rs. 1,000 crore is the 91-Day T-Bill / Overnight MIBOR trading-member floor and is not used at client level here. Rs. 300 crore reflects a different percentage that the workbook does not prescribe. Note: Per page 235, the exchange-level overall IRD open position on a specific underlying must not exceed 25% of the outstanding bond, but this is an exchange-level cap and separate from the open-interest-linked client limit applied here.
